title: Implement RBACv2 policy orchestration, CMK residency broker, and audit reconciliation
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers with strict data residency and operator scopes require a single control plane to coordinate RBACv2 policy decisions, per-tenant CMK (customer-managed key) residency constraints, and high-fidelity audit trails. This PR implements an orchestration layer that evaluates RBACv2 policy templates, enforces CMK residency constraints via a residency broker, and improves audit reconciliation to detect mismatches between decision logs and key usage.

What changed: Added rbac-orchestrator service (lightweight controller) that composes policy templates, an in-memory decision cache with TTL and invalidation hooks, and a CMK residency broker that mediates KMS provider selection based on tenant residency claims. The audit pipeline was extended to include decision_id correlation, key_origin metadata, and an audit-reconciliation worker that runs nightly to surface anomalies. Configuration changes include new feature flags (rbacv2_orchestrator_enabled, residency_broker_mode) and safe defaults for on-prem/private installations.

Design notes: The orchestrator implements a deterministic evaluation order: service-level allowlist -> tenant-scoped overrides -> operator-timebound grants. CMK residency broker matches tenant claims against KMS provider capabilities and returns a signed residency_assertion header for downstream services. Audit reconciliation performs delta comparisons between decision logs (rbac decisions) and KMS key usage events; discrepancies create low-priority tickets and telemetry events.

Files changed summary (high level) and rationale: small, targeted changes in authz/, kms/, audit/ and infra/ to keep runtime impact low. No changes to the public API surface except opt-in config flags and additional audit metadata emitted.

Testing and rollout: feature-flag gated rollout with staged canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and a fallback to previous policy evaluator if the orchestrator signals an error. Backward compatibility: when disabled the system uses legacy policy evaluator.

Related work: ENG-3421 (policy templates), SEC-881 (audit hardening).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Can the residency broker return a soft-fail mode when no matching CMK provider is available? Reply: Maya Chen: implemented a 'fallback_provider' config and documented behavior; broker will emit a telemetry event and fall back to region-agnostic managed key only when feature flag is off.

Priya Nair: Audit payload size grew—will this affect our ingestion pipeline? Reply: Maya Chen: added batching and a compressor step in audit/ingest and increased index throughput for the short window; load tests show <3% CPU increase on ingest nodes.
Samir Patel: Add a rate-limiter around the orchestrator evaluation to prevent cascading retries. Reply: Maya Chen: added token-bucket limiter, tests included.
Security review (Automated): verified that residency_assertion is signed with service key and validated at downstream call sites. Note: rotation guidance added to docs/security/rbacv2-orchestrator.md
release_notes: Adds RBACv2 orchestration and a CMK residency broker to enforce tenant key-residency constraints; audit logs now include decision_id and key_origin for improved traceability. Feature gated behind 'rbacv2_orchestrator_enabled'.
testing: unit: authz/orchestrator (100% coverage for core path)
load: canary runs up to 10k evals/min on GPU serving nodes
end-to-end: nightly reconcile job validated on staging for 7 days
rollout_plan: Enable feature flag for internal tenants (canary 10%) for 48h -> monitor reconcile alerts and latency -> 50% for 24h -> full enable. Emergency rollback: set feature flag false and restart orchestrator pods; orchestrator has health-check that reverts requests to legacy evaluator on error.
security_considerations: residency_assertion is cryptographically signed; rotation procedure documented
principle of least privilege enforced via operator-timebound grants
audit-reconciliation surfaces potential operator misuse or KMS misrouting
audit_log_changes_summary: Audit entries now include 'decision_id', 'policy_snapshot_hash', and 'key_origin' fields. Reconciliation worker cross-references decision logs with KMS usage events and emits a reconcile.alert when mismatches exceed threshold.
kms_integration_notes: Broker supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and local HSM via provider plugins
When multiple providers satisfy residency, selection order is: explicit tenant preference -> latency score -> cost score
Provider capability discovery runs periodically and is cached with TTL to avoid hot loops
